narrative.title: Calibrating Against an Unsorted Reference Chart
narrative.scenario: A lab calibrator compares a probe reading against a reference chart, but the chart was compiled from several technicians and its entries are out of order. The calibration needs two anchors: the closest reference value at or below the reading and the closest one at or above it. Bring the chart into order first, then locate both anchors, using -1 whenever an anchor does not exist.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n, an array arr of n integers in arbitrary order, and an integer x.
narrative.outputFormat: A pair [floor, ceil] of values: floor is the largest element at most x (or -1 if x is below every element) and ceil is the smallest element at least x (or -1 if x is above every element).

testCases.explanation: After ordering the chart, 6 is the deepest value not past 7 and 8 is the shallowest value not below it.
The reading matches a reference exactly, so both anchors collapse onto the same value 8.

hintLevels: Level 1: Binary search cannot run on unordered data, so one preparatory pass fixes that at a known cost.
Level 2: After sorting, run two carried-answer searches: one biased right for the largest value at most x, one biased left for the smallest value at least x.
Level 3: Both searches return positions that must be converted back into values, and either search can fail when x lies entirely outside the chart's range, which is why -1 is the sentinel.
